description: Phrase-aware rules that turn standing legal English into plain English. Every pattern is matched case-insensitively with word boundaries, so nothing is ever replaced inside an unrelated word. Rules run top to bottom: specific standing wording rewrites first, the generic wording at the bottom rewrites only what the specific rules left behind. No rule invents a fact; each one only re-states the same fact in plainer words.

phrase_rules.why: An adjournment postpones the hearing; it decides nothing.

phrase_rules.replacement: the hearing has started but is not finished
phrase_rules.why: Part-heard means the hearing began and will continue later.

phrase_rules.pattern: the matter is listed for hearing
phrase_rules.replacement: the case is scheduled for a hearing
phrase_rules.why: Listing means the court has put the case on its hearing list.
